title: Double Italian domination in trees
summary: Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V=V(G)$. A double Roman dominating function on a graph $G$ is a function $f : V \to \{0,1,2,3\}$ satisfying the conditions that if $f(v) = 0$, then vertex $v$ must have at least two neighbors in $V_2$ or one neighbor in $V_3$, if $f(v) = 1$, then vertex $v$ must have at least one neighbor in $V_2 \cup V_3$. The weight of a double Roman dominating function $f$ is the sum $f(V) = \sum_{v \in V} f(v)$, and the double Roman domination number $γ_{dR}(G)$ is the minimum weight of a double Roman dominating function on $G$.
